\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رنگین} \fa{کمان} (ranginkamân)}{رنگین کمان (ranginkamân)}]{\fa{رنگین} \fa{کمان} (ranginkamân) — a rainbow}

\label{lesson:FA-C479-ranginkaman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to dry up, then the Persian for foggy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رنگین} \fa{کمان}}
\textbf{\fa{رنگین} \fa{کمان}} (\emph{ranginkamân}) — \textquotedblleft{}a rainbow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{باران} \fa{یک} \fa{رنگین} \fa{کمان} \fa{در} \fa{آسمان} \fa{دیدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ba'd az bârân yek ranginkamân dar âsmân didim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the rain we saw a rainbow in the sky.
\end{quote}

Literally 'coloured bow': \emph{rangin} 'coloured' + \emph{kamân} 'bow'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ranginkamân} is a native compound of \emph{rangin} 'coloured', from \emph{rang} 'colour', and \emph{kamân} 'bow', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kamān} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ranginkamân}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ranginkamân}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ranginkamân}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to dry up, then the Persian for foggy, then say \emph{ranginkamân} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{رنگین} \fa{کمان} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A rainbow\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نسیم} (nasim)}{نسیم (nasim)}]{\fa{نسیم} (nasim) — a breeze}

\label{lesson:FA-C479-nasim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for foggy, then the Persian for a rainbow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نسیم}}
\textbf{\fa{نسیم}} (\emph{nasim}) — \textquotedblleft{}a breeze\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{عصر} \fa{نسیم} \fa{خنکی} \fa{از} \fa{دریا} \fa{میوزید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{'Asr nasim-e khonaki az daryâ mivazid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the afternoon a cool breeze was blowing from the sea.
\end{quote}

Also a given name, both for boys and girls.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nasim} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{nasīm}, which EtymDB lists; it is usually glossed 'a gentle breeze'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nasim}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nasim}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{nasim}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for foggy, then the Persian for a rainbow, then say \emph{nasim} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{درخشیدن} (derakhshidan)}{درخشیدن (derakhshidan)}]{\fa{درخشیدن} (derakhshidan) — to shine, to sparkle}

\label{lesson:FA-C479-derakhshidan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a rainbow, then the Persian for a breeze.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{درخشیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{درخشیدن}} (\emph{derakhshidan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to shine, to sparkle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{باران} \fa{خورشید} \fa{درخشید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ba'd az bârân khorshid derakhshid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the rain the sun shone.
\end{quote}

Present stem \emph{derakhsh-}: \emph{miderakhshad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{derakhshidan} is a native verb, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{draxšīdan} 'to shine'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{derakhshidan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{derakhshidan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{derakhshidan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a rainbow, then the Persian for a breeze, then say \emph{derakhshidan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{درخشیدن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To shine, to sparkle\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{غروب} \fa{کردن} (ghorub kardan)}{غروب کردن (ghorub kardan)}]{\fa{غروب} \fa{کردن} (ghorub kardan) — to set (of the sun)}

\label{lesson:FA-C479-ghorub-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a breeze, then the Persian for to shine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{غروب} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{غروب} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{ghorub kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to set (of the sun)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خورشید} \fa{پشت} \fa{کوه} \fa{غروب} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khorshid posht-e kuh ghorub kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sun set behind the mountain.
\end{quote}

\emph{ghorub} 'sunset' + \emph{kardan}. \emph{Ghorub} alone is sunset or dusk.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ghorub kardan} is built from \emph{ghorub} 'sunset', borrowed from Arabic \emph{ġurūb} (EtymDB), and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghorub kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghorub kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ghorub kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a breeze, then the Persian for to shine, then say \emph{ghorub kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{غروب} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To set (of the sun)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{طلوع} \fa{کردن} (tolu' kardan)}{طلوع کردن (tolu' kardan)}]{\fa{طلوع} \fa{کردن} (tolu' kardan) — to rise (of the sun or moon)}

\label{lesson:FA-C479-tolu-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to shine, then the Persian for to set.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{طلوع} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{طلوع} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tolu' kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to rise (of the sun or moon)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{صبح} \fa{زود} \fa{خورشید} \fa{از} \fa{پشت} \fa{دریا} \fa{طلوع} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sobh-e zud khorshid az posht-e daryâ tolu' kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Early in the morning the sun rose over the sea.
\end{quote}

\emph{tolu'} 'rising' + \emph{kardan}; the opposite of \emph{ghorub kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tolu' kardan} is built from \emph{tolu'} 'rising', borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṭulūʿ}, which EtymDB lists, and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tolu' kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tolu' kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tolu' kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to shine, then the Persian for to set, then say \emph{tolu' kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Shops, nature and weather — a review}

\label{lesson:FA-R479-review-476-479}



\begin{quote}
Say the Persian for a snowstorm and a blizzard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item muggy, humidity, heatstroke, mild, to sunbathe
  \item fine dust, dust, a drought, to dry up, foggy
  \item a rainbow, a breeze, to shine, to set, to rise
\end{itemize}

(\textbf{\fa{شرجی}}.) Humidity? (\textbf{\fa{رطوبت}}.) Heatstroke? (\textbf{\fa{گرمازدگی}}.) Mild? (\textbf{\fa{معتدل}}.) To sunbathe? (\textbf{\fa{آفتاب} \fa{گرفتن}}.) Fine dust? (\textbf{\fa{ریزگرد}}.) Dust? (\textbf{\fa{گرد} \fa{و} \fa{خاک}}.) A drought? (\textbf{\fa{خشکسالی}}.) To dry up? (\textbf{\fa{خشک} \fa{شدن}}.) Foggy? (\textbf{\fa{مه} \fa{آلود}}.) A rainbow? (\textbf{\fa{رنگین} \fa{کمان}}.) A breeze? (\textbf{\fa{نسیم}}.) To shine? (\textbf{\fa{درخشیدن}}.) To set? (\textbf{\fa{غروب} \fa{کردن}}.) To rise? (\textbf{\fa{طلوع} \fa{کردن}}.)
